title: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act — Further Extension Through June 12, 2026
official_title: A bill to amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
summary: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lets the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence jointly authorize, for up to one year at a time, the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information. They may do that on an order issued under subsection (j)(3), or on their own determination that exigent circumstances exist, and nothing in subchapter I of FISA requires an application for a court order for an acquisition targeted that way. The prohibitions the statute writes are specific rather than general: no intentional targeting of anyone known to be located in the United States, no targeting a person outside the United States in order to reach a particular known person here, no intentionally acquiring communications that contain a reference to, but are not to or from, a target, no intentionally acquiring a communication where the sender and all intended recipients are known to be in the United States, and the acquisition must be conducted consistent with the Fourth Amendment. FBI personnel may query what was collected using a U.S. person query term after prior approval from an FBI supervisor or attorney, unless they have a reasonable belief the query could assist in mitigating or eliminating a threat to life or serious bodily harm. This bill moves the repeal date for those authorities from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026 with no new limits or reforms added, and it was considered and passed by both chambers on April 30, 2026, the date they were otherwise set to lapse.
brief: Moves the repeal date for title VII of FISA, which contains Section 702, from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026, with no changes to oversight or limitations.

top_lines.headline: What Section 702 Allows
subs: The Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence authorize jointly, for up to one year at a time, the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information — on an order issued under subsection (j)(3), or on their own determination that exigent circumstances exist
Nothing in subchapter I of FISA is to be construed to require an application for a court order for an acquisition targeted at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States

The same two officials may direct an electronic communication service provider, in writing, to immediately provide the Government with all information, facilities, or assistance necessary to accomplish the acquisition, in a manner that will protect the secrecy of the acquisition and produce a minimum of interference with the services the provider is providing to the target

The acquisition may not intentionally target anyone known to be located in the United States, may not target a person outside the United States in order to reach a particular known person here, may not intentionally acquire communications that contain a reference to, but are not to or from, a target, may not intentionally acquire a communication where the sender and all intended recipients are known to be in the United States, and must be conducted consistent with the Fourth Amendment

FBI personnel must obtain prior approval from an FBI supervisor or attorney before a query of what was collected using a U.S. person query term, unless they have a reasonable belief the query could assist in mitigating or eliminating a threat to life or serious bodily harm; the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court reviews those querying procedures under subsection (j)

top_lines.headline: What This Extension Changes
subs: Repeal date moved from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026 — no new oversight requirements or limits added
Considered and passed by the Senate and the House on April 30, 2026 and approved the same day

sections.label: Section 1 — Extension of Title VII Authorities

items.main: Amends Section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to change the repeal date of Title VII authorities from April 30, 2026 to June 12, 2026.
items.detail: The same strike-and-insert is made twice: in paragraph (1) of Section 403(b), the 50 U.S.C. 1881 note, and in paragraph (2), the 18 U.S.C. 2511 note. Section 702 sits in title VII, added there by the same 2008 Act, so moving the title VII repeal date moves Section 702's with it. The amendments take effect on the earlier of the date of enactment or April 29, 2026.

underreported: The effective-date clause runs to the earlier of enactment or April 29, 2026 — a day before the April 30, 2026 deadline it replaces, so the new date is in force before the old one arrives.

criticisms.why: Mr. Speaker, it is nice to have the gentleman from Maryland on the pro-warrant side of this conversation this go-round. I will note that there was a significant amount of abuses by the previous President with respect to the amount of focus on the American people using FISA and the abuses therein. I hope we can achieve a bipartisan consensus here on how we reform this regardless of who is in the White House and regardless of who controls Congress. We need to do that in defense of the Constitution.

Mr. Speaker, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is a fine tool for foreign intelligence. Unfortunately, it has been abused and corrupted. I am encouraged to hear Mr. Raskin reclaim his opposition to warrantless surveillance, and I am encouraged that there is a bipartisan effort to reform it. In fact, I think the will of this body is that we defend the Constitution and we defend this Nation. We can do both. We are presented this false dilemma that somehow if you just abandon your freedom, you can be more secure. That is a false tradeoff.

Mr. Speaker, everyone here wants 702 reauthorized. The case has been made that it is a national security issue, that our troops on the ground need it. They need the intelligence that it provides. We want the CIA and the NSA to run as fast and as far as they can to identify the bad guys. I have deployed on three continents, and believe you me, we want our military to know who to deal with when they get on foreign soil. The FBI has abused 702, and that is why we are here today.

gaps: The bill sets a June 12, 2026 expiration date but establishes no conditions, reporting requirements, or reform benchmarks governing what happens at that expiration.
The bill title references additional purposes beyond the extension, but the text contains only the extension — no other changes to FISA are made.
